concepts.title: Steps for Problem Solving
concepts.definition: Solving a task on a computer runs through four stages: analyse the statement to pin down inputs and outputs, draft an algorithm, translate it into a program (coding), then test and debug until every kind of input yields the right output.
concepts.key_idea: Garbage in, garbage out: a wrong input analysis poisons every later stage of the solution.
question_patterns: Name the four key stages of problem solving and say what happens in each.
Why must a problem be analysed before any code is written?
What is the difference between a syntax error and a logical error during testing?
List the kinds of testing that the software industry applies to a large application.
A program runs but prints wrong totals. Which stage was flawed and how will you locate it?

solution_steps.action: walk the four stages in order
solution_steps.explain: Each stage depends on the previous one: analysis fixes inputs and outputs, the algorithm fixes the method, coding fixes the language form, and testing plus debugging fixes the correctness.

worked_examples.q: What is the first stage of solving a task on a computer?

concepts.title: Area and Perimeter of a Rectangle
concepts.definition: A first algorithm records its input, states the processing and names the output; for a rectangle the processing multiplies length by breadth for area, and doubles the sum of the sides for perimeter.
concepts.key_idea: Every algorithm should begin by fixing three things: the input accepted, the processing done, and the output printed.
question_patterns: Write pseudocode to compute the area and perimeter of a rectangle from its length and breadth.
A field measures 25 m by 12 m. Compute its area and the length of fencing needed around it.
In the rectangle algorithm, which line represents the processing step?
Draw a flowchart symbol sequence for input, process and output of a rectangle's area.
A rectangle's area is 180 square units and its length is 15 units. Find its breadth and then its perimeter.

solution_steps.explain: Area multiplies the two side lengths.
A rectangle has two lengths and two breadths.

worked_examples.q: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter in cm?

concepts.title: Average of Five Numbers with a Counter Loop
concepts.definition: A counting loop reads one number per pass, adds it to a running total, and bumps a counter; when the counter reaches the loop limit, the total divided by the count of values gives the average.
concepts.key_idea: The counter both decides when the loop ends and records how many values entered the total.
question_patterns: Five readings 6, 7, 4, 8 and 2 enter the loop of Example 4.8. What average is printed?
Why is a counter incremented inside every pass of the loop?
Write pseudocode that accepts 5 numbers and prints their average.
In the averaging loop, what happens if the counter is never incremented?
A loop collects 8 numbers whose total is 96. What value is printed at the end?

solution_steps.explain: Each pass folds one more number into the running total.
solution_steps.compute: total = n1 + n2 + n3 + n4 + n5

solution_steps.explain: The counter equals 5 after the loop, so divide the total by it.

worked_examples.q: Five test scores total 360. What is their average?

concepts.title: Selection with Conditionals: Even or Odd
concepts.definition: Selection lets an algorithm pick between two paths by testing a condition that evaluates to true or false; testing the remainder on division by 2 routes a number to the even or the odd branch.
concepts.key_idea: A zero remainder after dividing by 2 signals an even number; anything else signals odd.
question_patterns: Write pseudocode that prints whether an entered number is even or odd.
The number 17 enters the parity test. Which branch executes and why?
What value does number MOD 2 return for 24?
Which flowchart symbol represents the even-or-odd decision point?
Rewrite the even-or-odd test using an if-else block and state the output for 0.

solution_steps.action: test the remainder on division by 2
solution_steps.explain: MOD returns 0 for even numbers and 1 for odd ones.

solution_steps.action: flip it into an even flag
solution_steps.explain: Adding 1 and taking MOD 2 again turns 0 into 1 for even and 1 into 0 for odd.

worked_examples.q: What remainder does 14 leave on division by 2 -- the test that separates even from odd?

concepts.title: Dry Run of a Time-Adding Algorithm
concepts.definition: Verifying an algorithm means walking through its steps with sample inputs, called a dry run; adding two durations exposes a missing carry when the minutes cross 60, which the corrected algorithm folds into the hours.
concepts.key_idea: A dry run with a case that crosses the boundary, such as 70 minutes, is what reveals a missing carry step.
question_patterns: Add 4 hours 50 minutes and 2 hours 20 minutes using the corrected algorithm and state the result.
Why did the first time-adding algorithm fail for 4 h 50 min plus 2 h 20 min?
What is a dry run and why is it performed on an algorithm?
An algorithm must add 3 h 45 m and 1 h 30 m. Compute the correct total.
How should an algorithm adjust the minutes when their sum reaches 60 or more?

solution_steps.explain: Minute parts add first and may cross 59.
Every full 60 minutes is one extra hour.
The remainder after removing full hours stays in the minutes column.
Add both hour parts and the carry.

worked_examples.q: A dry run adds 2 h 45 min and 1 h 30 min. How many minutes pile up before the carry into hours?

concepts.title: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
concepts.definition: The total of the numbers from 1 to N has a closed form: multiply N by N plus one and halve the product; small cases such as N equals 6 give 21, which is how the formula is verified by hand.
concepts.key_idea: Checking a formula against small manually computed cases is the simplest way to verify it.
question_patterns: Using the formula N times N plus one over 2, find the sum of the first 10 natural numbers.
Verify the sum formula for N = 6 by listing the numbers and adding them.
What is the sum of the first 100 natural numbers?
The first N natural numbers total 55. Find N.
Why is verifying a formula with small values useful before coding it?

solution_steps.explain: The closed form pairs N with N plus 1.
Every pair was counted twice, so divide by 2.

worked_examples.q: Using the closed formula, what is the sum of the first 100 natural numbers?

concepts.title: Prime Testing and Algorithm Complexity
concepts.definition: A prime check can test divisors up to the number, up to half of it, or only up to its square root; each refinement cuts the divisibility trials, which is exactly the trade-off captured by time complexity and, when a prime list is stored, space complexity.
concepts.key_idea: Two algorithms that agree on the answer can still differ hugely in processing time and memory use.
question_patterns: Why is it enough to test divisibility only up to the square root of a number?
For the number 97, how many candidate divisors are skipped by moving from half-of-N to square-root-of-N testing?
Define time complexity and space complexity of an algorithm.
Rank the four prime-testing methods of section 4.7 from slowest to fastest.
What extra resource does the fourth prime-testing method spend to save calculations?
A number 1009 is tested for primality. Compute its square-root testing limit.

solution_steps.explain: Method two tests every divisor up to half the number.
Method three stops at the square root, floored to a whole divisor.
The skipped trials equal the difference of the two limits.

worked_examples.q: A prime check tests divisors from 2 up to a number's square root. For 101, how many divisor checks happen at most?

concepts.title: Decomposition of Complex Problems
concepts.definition: Decomposition splits a complex job, like a railway reservation system, into smaller sub-problems that can be solved and tested separately, often by different teams, and then joined into one working whole.
concepts.key_idea: Divide and conquer: each sub-problem is easier than the original and can be assigned to specialist teams.
question_patterns: What is decomposition, and why does it suit a railway reservation system?
Name three sub-problems into which a reservation system could be split.
Why can different teams work on different sub-problems at the same time?
After the sub-problems are solved, what must happen before the whole system works?
Give two everyday situations where decomposition is a natural strategy.

solution_steps.explain: Break the task into independent sub-problems, solve and test each one, then combine them so the parts interact correctly.

worked_examples.q: Splitting a railway reservation system into booking, payment and printing parts is called what?

worked_examples.title: Dry run of adding two durations
worked_examples.problem: A journey leg takes 4 h 50 min and the next leg 2 h 20 min. Apply the corrected time-adding algorithm to get the total duration.

steps.explain: Ten minutes remain after the carry.

worked_examples.answer_note: The total journey time is 7 hours 10 minutes.

worked_examples.title: Water bill with slab rates
worked_examples.problem: A household consumes 350 units in a month. The first 100 units cost 5 per unit, the next 150 cost 10 per unit, units beyond 250 cost 20 per unit, and a fixed meter charge of 75 is added. Compute the bill.

steps.explain: Three slabs plus the meter charge.

worked_examples.answer_note: The month's water bill comes to 500 plus 1500 plus 2000 plus 75, that is 4075.
